analysis.title: The AI boom is hiding something extraordinary
key_insights: AI dominates US equity returns, earnings growth and investment spending, while most stocks struggle and the economy depends more on a single investment cycle.
JPM: the S&P 500 is near record highs, but roughly 60% of its constituents trade more than 20% below their own all-time highs. Mega-cap winners are masking weakness across much of the market.

GS: US fundamental long/short net exposure is in the 2nd percentile of the past five years while the S&P 500 is near record highs. Hedge funds are crowded in AI and mega-cap winners but light on the broader market, which could provide buying power on meaningful dips.

BofA: US GDP from computers and peripheral equipment is projected at $401bn in Q2'26, up from $145bn in Q3'23. That is a near-tripling in under three years, and the bond market is being asked to fund it.
AI demand for capital could change the economics of borrowing for everyone else, and rising bond yields threaten the economics of the boom.

JPM (Cembalest): since January 2024, tech returns across major global markets have been driven mainly by earnings growth rather than multiple expansion. This complicates the bubble argument but does not remove downside risk if earnings expectations disappoint.

Variant Perception 'Juniper Networks' analog: Cisco peaked in March 2000 while Juniper peaked in October 2000 as late-stage IPOs absorbed liquidity from earlier leaders. Nvidia is holding up while second-tier names have drawn down. CoreWeave is about half its 2025 high and SpaceX is about 25% below its post-IPO peak. With Anthropic and OpenAI delaying IPOs, the public equity market may be running out of marginal buyers.
GS: CTAs have been aggressively selling gold. The last time systematic positioning was this bearish, gold reversed sharply higher, so a squeeze setup is possible.

GS (McGeoch): buying duration only works if yields are close to peaking. If that is the view, gold is a cleaner expression of the same trade, given structural support from the PBOC and other central banks while bonds face fiscal risks and heavy government borrowing.
GS: Brazil is one of the hottest EM trades. EWZ has broken out of a multi-year range with accelerating ETF inflows, though short-term risk/reward is harder to assess after the rally.

GS: Brazil has the highest real rates in the world and the strongest negative correlation between equities and local 5-year yields across EM. If the expected easing cycle accelerates, Brazilian equities could have more upside than the recent rally suggests.

sector_views.rationale: Elevated valuations and extreme concentration, but returns since January 2024 are driven by earnings growth rather than multiple expansion (JPM Cembalest). Variant Perception flags late-cycle liquidity risk.

earnings_insights: Tech-sector returns across major global markets since January 2024 were driven predominantly by earnings growth rather than multiple expansion (JPM Cembalest). No specific EPS or revenue figures are given.

macro_indicators.indicator: US GDP contribution from computers and peripheral equipment (AI hardware capex proxy)
macro_indicators.interpretation: A near-tripling in under three years. The bond market is being asked to fund the build-out, so higher yields raise the cost of the AI investment cycle.

trade_ideas.description: Long gold instead of long-duration bonds as the expression of a view that yields are near a peak (GS McGeoch)
trade_ideas.rationale: Both benefit from a turn in rates, but gold has structural central-bank support (PBOC and others) while bonds face fiscal risks and heavy government borrowing.

trade_ideas.description: Long Brazil equities via EWZ, on the breakout, ETF inflows and high real rates (GS)
trade_ideas.rationale: Brazil has the highest real rates in the world and the strongest negative equity-to-local-5-year-yield correlation in EM, so an accelerating easing cycle could extend the rally.
trade_ideas.risk: Short-term risk/reward is harder to assess after the powerful rally.

risk_factors: Rising bond yields could change the economics of the AI boom and raise borrowing costs for everyone else.
Extreme concentration: a narrow group of mega-cap winners masks weakness in about 60% of S&P 500 constituents.
Earnings expectations disappointing would expose elevated tech valuations.
The public equity market may be running out of marginal buyers as Anthropic and OpenAI delay IPOs (Variant Perception).
Bond market funding of AI capex and fiscal risks from government borrowing.

tension_points.bull_case: Since January 2024, tech returns across major global markets have been driven predominantly by earnings growth rather than multiple expansion (JPM Cembalest). Hedge fund net exposure is in the 2nd percentile, leaving buying power on dips (GS).
tension_points.bear_case: Valuations are elevated, concentration is extreme and about 60% of S&P 500 stocks are in bear markets (JPM). Variant Perception sees a Juniper-style analog with second-tier names already down and IPOs delayed, so marginal buyers may be running out. Rising bond yields threaten the economics of AI capex funding (BofA).
tension_points.what_invalidates: Earnings expectations disappointing, per the report: the earnings-driven case weakens if expectations are missed.
